Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Town, shops & places

police noun

also the police, police force, chief of police

classical

Traupman 191, 193
Suet. Aug. 30 (Lewis & Short s.v. vigil)

vigilēs, vigilum m. pl.

noun, third declension, plural

the police; classically the watch

Augustus’ seven cohorts of the watch, Rome’s night police and fire brigade (Lewis & Short); Traupman’s word for the police. Their commander, the praefectus vigilum, is his chief of police (p. 194).

Other words

  • pūblicae sēcūritātis custōdēs — guardians of public safety: police officers

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. policeman (Egger); Levi–Bini p. 49: cūrātōrēs pūblicae disciplīnae (or sēcūritātis)

    Egger’s name for a police officer, in the plural.

  • praefectus vigilum — chief of police (the prefect of the watch)

    also used · classical · Traupman 290

Examples

  • Arcessīvistīne vigilēs? — Arcessīvī.

    Did you call the police? — I did.Traupman 193

  • vigilēs, quī custōdiēbant vīcīnam regiōnem, ratī ārdēre Trimalchiōnis domum, effrēgērunt jānuam subitō

    the watch, who were guarding the neighbourhood, thought Trimalchio’s house was on fire and suddenly broke the door downPetr. 78

  • praefectus vigilum

    the chief of policeTraupman 194

See also police officer, police station, firefighter.
